target_customer: Regulated organizations and enterprises needing compliance and legal rules applied deterministically to processes
problem: LLM answers on legal and compliance questions are probabilistic; organizations need deterministic, auditable application of rules that change over time.
product_category: computational law and compliance knowledge layer

founders.name: Joe Savidge
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: two-time startup first product hire.

founders.name: Shav Vimalendiran
founders.background_notes: Built an institutional trading platform; published LLM alignment researcher per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Encoding legal and regulatory rules into machine-executable, interpretable form and keeping them updated is hard; founders have quant and Palantir backgrounds.

defensibility.rationale: A maintained rules knowledge base could compound, but unproven; no customers named.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: General legal AI vendors grew quickly in 2025 but target research and drafting; no direct copy of deterministic computational law found.

market_need_then: Enterprises distrust LLM hallucination in compliance contexts; regulation changes continuously.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical: deterministic, interpretable legal and compliance AI

brand_strength.rationale: No press or brand coverage; searches returned unrelated SAM Labs and other SAMMY trademark holders.

outcome_analysis: SAMMY Labs is an active London based Winter 2025 YC company building deterministic computational law for compliance. Public evidence is thin: no named customers, no verified funding round and no reported exit or shutdown. It is too early to attribute success or failure factors, and positioning against fast growing LLM legal tools is the main open risk.
notes: VCBacked, PitchBook and Standout give about $500K (Feb 2025, YC and Pioneer Fund, PitchBook adds Antler and others); aggregators only, unverified, not recorded as a round. Competitor search returned only generic legal AI vendors (Harvey, Legora, Norm Ai) with no dated source near the batch tied to computational law, so the list is empty. A search snippet suggested a possible pivot to app testing, from a YC job page; unverified. Founding engineer Josh Carey is listed on the YC page but not as a co-founder. Completeness pass: the Feb 2025 pre-seed of about $500K now rests on a single database (VCBacked); Preqin instead says an undisclosed seed from Pioneer Fund in March 2025, and PitchBook adds Antler per earlier notes. No press total found.
